Subject: Embedding runtime onboarding & batch strategy — next steps

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can kick off the integration sprint:

Summary of what we heard
- You currently use VectorCloud for embeddings (approx 1024 dim), serving a semantic search index for product search and recommendations.
- Goals: reduce per-query latency, lower token/compute cost for similarity lookups, and consolidate embedding pipeline to one vendor.
- Constraints: 30M historic vectors, nightly re-indexing window, strict throughput during peak (US East).

Redwood recommendations (high-level)
- Embedding dimension: we recommend testing our 1536-d variant (higher recall) plus a smaller 768-d variant for cost-sensitive slices. Start POC with 1536 on a representative sample.
- Normalization: use L2 normalization at write-time to ensure cosine similarity == dot-product performance in our runtime.
- Batching: for bulk migration ingest, aim for batches of 128–256 vectors per request; for live traffic, prefer small batches (<= 16) to keep tail latency low.
- Migration approach: two-phase — 1) bulk re-embed historical corpus (batch pipeline), 2) canary live traffic (routing by user cohort / path) and gradual cutover. We can provide a migration playbook and an example worker.

Technical next steps (owners & timeline)
- Redwood: provide sample SDK auth snippet, an embed schema xlsx, and migration playbook (attaching). (Owner: Aditya) — deliver by Thu, 6/30.
- Pinecrest: share a 1% representative dataset and preferred S3 location for bulk upload. (Owner: Alex) — target by Fri, 7/2.
- TW: schedule a 60-minute hands-on onboarding + workshop focused on SDK setup, service-account auth, routing rules, and a short test run. (Owner: Olga) — propose slots below.

Attachments: embed-schema-v1.xlsx (schema + sample rows), Pinecrest migration playbook (high level).

Proposed workshop slots
- Wed 7/7 10:00–11:00 ET
- Thu 7/8 14:00–15:00 ET

If that looks good we'll trigger Aditya to prepare the SDK snippets and a short Docker-based test harness so you can run a small canary in your environment.

Hi Alex — looping in a few technical details and pragmatic plans. Answers inline: 

1) Dimension mapping / migration- Short answer: there is no lossless projection from 1024->1536 that preserves semantic geometry reliably for production. Options: 
  - Re-embed historical corpus (recommended for best quality). Bulk re-embed can be run in parallel across workers; Redwood supports streaming bulk ingest via our SDK with backpressure.
  - Partial migration / hybrid: keep 1024 for cold archive + re-embed frequently accessed items to 1536. Maintain mapping table (old_id -> new_vector) and a flag to route queries to the appropriate vector table.

2) Normalization- Write-time L2 normalization is recommended. If you currently normalize at query-time only, moving to write-time L2 will not break cosine similarity (it makes queries faster since we can do raw dot products). We can add a quick compatibility shim in the canary that applies the same normalization at read-time during the transition window.

3) Auth & SDK- We support both long-lived API keys and short-lived service tokens via OIDC integration. For GCP customers we can mint short-lived tokens using a linked service account and Redwood's token exchange endpoint (RBAC scopes available). Sample (pseudo) flow:
  - Create a Redwood service principal in Console -> assign minimal scopes (embeddings:write, embeddings:read).
  - Use your existing IAM to exchange for a short-lived Redwood token (we provide an exchange endpoint).
  - SDK accepts bearer token in Authorization header.

4) Routing / fallback- Per-request routing is supported in the SDK. You can set a routing header (x-redwood-routing: variant=canary) to select model/cluster. If the canary cluster is overloaded we support automatic fallback to the primary cluster or to a configured external endpoint. We'll share an example policy that does percentage-based routing + an automatic fallback to VectorCloud endpoints.

Performance & batching guidance-
  - Bulk re-embed: worker concurrency 24–48, batch size 128–256 vectors, parallel streams to utilize GPU pools efficiently.
  - Live requests: batch up to 16 vectors to keep p95 latency under 120ms (depending on payload size and seq length).
  - Normalization + quantization: do L2 normalization at write-time; we recommend keeping float32 for the first pass during the POC, then layer post-POC quantization if memory/cost becomes a constraint.

Attachments we will deliver (by EoD Thu): embed-schema-v1.xlsx, migration_playbook.pdf, SDK snippet + OIDC exchange example, routing-policy-example.json.

Proposed immediate steps
- Olga: confirm workshop slot (Thu 7/8 14:00 ET).
- Alex: share sample 1% dataset and S3 prefix.
- Pinecrest SRE: confirm whether you want us to run a short-lived token integration or start with API key for the workshop.

Happy to jump on a 30-minute pre-workshop call if you want a quick walk-through of the SDK.

— Aditya
